references.text: Aaron and his sons were chosen for priestly service, and here the holy garments to be made for them are described.
The instructions for the consecration of Aaron and his sons, including the sin offering (the bull) and the two rams mentioned in Leviticus 8:2.
The anointing oil (שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה) is used to consecrate Aaron and his sons for priestly service.
The recipe for the holy anointing oil and instructions on its use to consecrate priests and the sanctuary.
The dressing of Aaron with the holy garments that were gathered in verse 2.
The sin offering bull (פַּר הַחַטָּאת) that was gathered in verse 2 is sacrificed here.
The first ram (the burnt offering ram) of the two rams mentioned in verse 2 is sacrificed.
The basket of unleavened bread (סַל הַמַּצּוֹת) that was gathered in verse 2 is used in the consecration ritual.
The unleavened bread, the unleavened cakes with oil, and the unleavened flatbreads - parallel to the basket of unleavened bread.
Hebrews explains that the high priest is chosen from among people to serve on behalf of the people, just as Aaron was called.
